mechanisms.label: Robotics decoupling
mechanisms.summary: The U.S. has enacted a trade barrier that restricts imports of new Chinese robotics, specifically humanoid and connected mobile robots, citing national security and cybersecurity concerns. The policy is part of a broader effort to decouple Western robotics supply chains from China. The regulation applies to new models that cannot obtain FCC equipment authorizations unless they receive conditional approval, and it also imposes tariff pressures on components sourced from China. This policy is expected to benefit domestic U.S. robotics manufacturers and suppliers that can meet the domestic content thresholds, while disadvantaging Chinese robotics firms and those heavily reliant on Chinese components.
